tool_args.old_string: \looseness=-1 CIVO is an emergent property of co-adapting embeddings, not a single-pathway defect: SGS fails from pathway redundancy; RAVE fails as the EMA anchor tracks biased values; TCN shows binary behavior suggesting a phase transition. The only reliable elimination, freezing the embedding (0/16 controls), degrades performance to 22--33\% of baseline. Wide dual-critic achieves prevention in 3/4 seeds (NVE $\leq 1.4\times$), though Cheetah transfer fails (0/1, CIVO at $108\times$). These findings generalize beyond DreamerV3: embedding co-adaptation may interact pathologically with value estimation in any imagination-based actor-critic that bootstraps within a learned model.
tool_args.new_string: \looseness=-1 CIVO is an emergent property of co-adapting embeddings, not a single-pathway defect: SGS fails from pathway redundancy; RAVE fails as the EMA anchor tracks biased values; TCN shows binary behavior suggesting a phase transition. The only reliable elimination, freezing the embedding (0/16 controls), degrades performance to 22--33\% of baseline. At the architecture level, the $2{\times}2$ critic factorial shows that min-aggregation enables recovery but not prevention; their combination achieves prevention in 3/4 seeds (NVE $\leq 1.4\times$), though Cheetah transfer failure (0/1, CIVO at $108\times$) suggests a severity ceiling. CIVO is specific to moderate-complexity locomotion across both tested environments (5/7 seeds; Appendix~\ref{sec:cross_env_appendix}). These findings generalize beyond DreamerV3: embedding co-adaptation may interact pathologically with value estimation in any imagination-based actor-critic that bootstraps within a learned model.

Cross-environment validation on Cheetah confirms CIVO generalization (010b, NVE $8.27$--$108.52\times$); full-SGS yields 0/3 elimination. Removing the embedding eliminates CIVO on Cheetah (024b, NVE $< 0.2\times$). Targeted obs-decoder-only SGS (exp\_025/026) achieves 1/6 prevention (1/4 Walker, 0/2 Cheetah; Table~\ref{tab:intervention_hierarchy}), confirming pathway redundancy: blocking the dominant channel shifts co-adaptation to remaining pathways (Appendix~\ref{sec:seed_divergence}).
tool_args.new_string: \looseness=-1 Full-SGS (exp\_018) detaches all non-KL gradients from $e_{\dt}$. Seed~1 shows partial mitigation (eval 448.3, NVE $1.66\times$) with late instability---NVE rising from $1.23\times$ mean to $1.66\times$ at 95K---suggesting SGS delays rather than prevents onset; seed~2 collapses entirely (peak ${\sim}488$ at 75K $\to$ 40.8 at 105K; Appendix~\ref{sec:sgs_gradient_analysis}). The seed divergence indicates that full-SGS creates a metastable regime where stochastic factors determine whether delayed onset crosses the critical threshold within the training horizon. Cross-environment validation on Cheetah confirms CIVO generalization (010b, NVE $8.27$--$108.52\times$); full-SGS yields 0/3 elimination. Removing the embedding eliminates CIVO on Cheetah (024b, NVE $< 0.2\times$). Targeted obs-decoder-only SGS (exp\_025/026) achieves 1/6 prevention (1/4 Walker, 0/2 Cheetah; Table~\ref{tab:intervention_hierarchy}), confirming pathway redundancy: blocking the dominant gradient channel shifts co-adaptation to remaining pathways (Appendix~\ref{sec:seed_divergence}).

1	\looseness=-1 World-model reinforcement learning increasingly targets continuous control tasks where temporal abstraction enables planning across heterogeneous time scales. We find that $\Delta t$-conditioning, effective in model-predictive control (MPC), cannot transfer to imagination-based actor-critic training: every variable-rate DreamerV3 configuration suffers substantial performance degradation. Factorial diagnostics on two continuous-control tasks identify the combination of trained temporal embedding and multi-rate data exposure as the strongest predictor of this failure, \emph{conditioning-induced value overestimation} (CIVO; AUROC${=}1.000$, $n{=}36$), with cross-environment validation on four additional tasks confirming specificity to moderate-complexity locomotion. The recurrent state-space model (RSSM) develops a reward prediction gap at $\Delta t{>}1$ that the critic internalizes as optimistic values; the contrast with MPC identifies feedback architecture as a hypothesized structural factor. Gradient, output, and representation interventions fail to eliminate CIVO; at the architecture level, dual critics converge in pure imagination, but wide dual-critic (min-aggregation $+$ increased capacity) achieves partial prevention, the only positive result, highlighting open challenges in the architectural design of variable-rate model-based RL.

**Title**: Why Temporal Abstraction Can Fail in Imagination-Based RL: A Diagnostic Analysis of Variable-Rate DreamerV3

**Abstract**: World-model reinforcement learning increasingly targets continuous control tasks where temporal abstraction enables planning across heterogeneous time scales. We find that Δt-conditioning, effective in model-predictive control (MPC), cannot transfer to imagination-based actor-critic training: every variable-rate DreamerV3 configuration suffers substantial performance degradation. Factorial diagnostics on two continuous-control tasks identify the combination of trained temporal embedding and multi-rate data exposure as the strongest predictor of this failure, conditioning-induced value overestimation (CIVO; AUROC=1.000, n=36), with cross-environment validation on four additional tasks confirming specificity to moderate-complexity locomotion. The recurrent state-space model (RSSM) develops a reward prediction gap at Δt>1 that the critic internalizes as optimistic values; the contrast with MPC identifies feedback architecture as a hypothesized structural factor. Gradient, output, and representation interventions fail to eliminate CIVO; at the architecture level, dual critics converge in pure imagination, but wide dual-critic (min-aggregation + increased capacity) achieves partial prevention, the only positive result, highlighting open challenges in the architectural design of variable-rate model-based RL.

**Primary Keyword**: Model-based and model-free learning for robotic control
